body:
Countertops take more abuse than any other part of a casework package. The right material depends on how the space is used, how it's cleaned and what the budget allows. Here's how the three materials we fabricate most often compare.

## Plastic laminate (HPL)

High-pressure laminate bonded to a stable core is the workhorse of commercial casework.

- **Best for:** offices, classrooms, break rooms and other general-use spaces.
- **Strengths:** lowest cost, hundreds of colors and patterns, quick to fabricate and replace.
- **Watch for:** visible seams on long runs, and damage from standing water at unsealed edges or direct heat.

## Solid surface

A non-porous acrylic or polyester material that can be joined with nearly invisible seams.

- **Best for:** healthcare, labs, restrooms and anywhere hygiene matters.
- **Strengths:** seamless tops with integral sinks and backsplashes, and scratches can be sanded out and repaired in place.
- **Watch for:** it's softer than stone, so it can scratch or scorch, and it costs more than laminate.

## Quartz

Engineered stone made mostly of crushed quartz and resin.

- **Best for:** reception desks, hospitality, food service fronts and high-visibility spaces.
- **Strengths:** very hard, stain-resistant, low-maintenance, and a premium look.
- **Watch for:** the highest cost of the three, heavier weight, visible seams on long runs, and it shouldn't take direct heat.

## Quick comparison

- **Budget:** laminate, then solid surface, then quartz.
- **Hygiene and seamless sinks:** solid surface.
- **Durability and appearance:** quartz.
- **Fastest turnaround:** laminate.

Not sure which fits your project? [Ask our team](/contact). We'll recommend the right material for how the space will actually be used.
summary: Each countertop material has a place in commercial work. Here's how plastic laminate, solid surface and quartz compare on cost, durability, cleaning and repairs.

title: Plastic laminate, solid surface or quartz: choosing commercial countertops
